source.paraphrase: The Unsafe raw methods run the string as SQL. Values are safe only as extra arguments bound to $1 placeholders; text built into the string is not parameterized.

invariants.why: SQL built at runtime and passed to an Unsafe call puts caller input straight into the query, so one malicious value owns it.
invariants.fixHint: Switch to the $queryRaw or $executeRaw template form and interpolate values with ${}, or keep a constant SQL string with $1 placeholders and pass the values as extra arguments.
invariants.avoid: Wrapping the string in a helper or awaiting the call does not parameterize it. A bare variable or an interpolated template is still runtime SQL. A constant string literal with $n placeholders passes; values given as extra arguments are bound.

source.locator: section on template versus string arguments to $queryRaw
source.paraphrase: Only the template form of $queryRaw and $executeRaw parameterizes values. A plain string argument is sent as-is, so concatenation reopens injection.

invariants.why: String concatenation inside a raw call builds SQL by hand, defeating the parameterization the template form would have applied.
invariants.fixHint: Rewrite the call as a template literal and interpolate each value with ${} instead of concatenating.
invariants.avoid: $executeRaw has the same hole as $queryRaw. A constant string with no concatenation is fine and stays green.

relations.why: $queryRaw(Prisma.raw("..." + value)) is reported by both rules: this one sees + in the raw call's arguments, PRISMA-RAW-002 sees the assembled Prisma.raw text.
relations.settle: Keep both. Moving the value into a $queryRaw tagged template or Prisma.sql satisfies both; PRISMA-RAW-002 also covers Prisma.raw fragments built outside the raw call.

source.locator: SQL injection prevention, unsafe use of $queryRaw and $executeRaw (misuse of Prisma.raw); https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/prisma-client/using-raw-sql/raw-queries#sql-injection-prevention
source.paraphrase: Prisma.raw inserts its text into the query unescaped. The docs list Prisma.raw over an interpolated template as vulnerable to SQL injection, and use Prisma.sql or the tagged template for values.

invariants.why: Prisma.raw turns its text into SQL syntax. A value interpolated or concatenated into that text escapes parameterization, even inside an otherwise safe $queryRaw template.
invariants.fixHint: Pass the value as ${value} in a $queryRaw tagged template or Prisma.sql, so it travels as a parameter. Keep Prisma.raw for constant fragments or identifiers chosen from a fixed allowlist.
invariants.avoid: Nesting Prisma.raw inside a $queryRaw tagged template does not parameterize its text. The rule sees a template with ${} or + in the first Prisma.raw argument; Prisma.raw(variable) passes because an allowlisted identifier and raw input look the same here.

relations.why: Prisma.raw(`...${value}`) is a raw method with an interpolated first argument, so both rules report it.
relations.settle: Keep both. A $queryRaw tagged template or Prisma.sql satisfies both; PRISMA-RAW-002 also catches + concatenation.

relations.why: $queryRaw(Prisma.raw("..." + value)) is reported by both rules: PRISMA-SQL-001 sees + in the raw call's arguments, this one sees the assembled Prisma.raw text.
relations.settle: Keep both. Moving the value into a $queryRaw tagged template or Prisma.sql satisfies both.

source.locator: section on include with nested select
source.paraphrase: include with `: true` loads the whole related record. Nesting a select keeps the join but fetches only the named fields.

invariants.why: A full-relation include pulls every column of every related row, including fields the caller never reads and should never see.
invariants.fixHint: Replace `: true` with a nested select naming the fields the caller needs, or add take to bound the relation.
invariants.avoid: Pushing `: true` one level down under a nested include is the same over-fetch. select without include is already scoped. Prisma documents include with `: true` as a supported query, so this stays advisory: whether the extra columns matter depends on the caller.

source.paraphrase: findFirst without an orderBy returns whichever row the database happens to visit first. An explicit order makes the pick deterministic.

invariants.why: Without an order the same query returns different rows across replicas, vacuums, and plan changes, so behavior drifts silently.
invariants.fixHint: Add an orderBy that names the winner, such as createdAt descending. Keep it on both findFirst and findFirstOrThrow.
invariants.avoid: OrThrow only changes the missing-row case. It does not order anything.

source.locator: section on instantiating PrismaClient per request
source.paraphrase: Each PrismaClient owns a connection pool. Constructing one per request exhausts the database, so handlers must share a singleton.

invariants.why: A fresh client per request opens a fresh pool per request, and the database runs out of connections under load.
invariants.fixHint: Import one shared client and keep it on globalThis. On Prisma ORM 7, construct it with a driver adapter (new PrismaClient({ adapter })) or accelerateUrl for Accelerate. https://www.prisma.io/docs/guides/upgrade-prisma-orm/v7
invariants.avoid: Exporting the new client from the route file still builds one pool per route module. The singleton module itself is the only place that may construct.

source.locator: section on the query log level
source.paraphrase: The query log level emits every SQL statement with its bound parameters. Production clients should log errors, not queries.

invariants.why: Query logs carry raw SQL and bound values into log storage, leaking personal data and query structure to anyone with log access.
invariants.fixHint: Set log to error only, or drop the log option. Keep query logging behind a local debug flag.
invariants.avoid: Appending error next to query keeps the query stream. The object form with level query is the same leak.

source.paraphrase: Prisma ORM 7 removes the client middleware API. The upgrade guide replaces prisma.$use with a client extension created by $extends.

invariants.why: On Prisma ORM 7 the $use call throws at runtime, so the query behavior it used to wrap never runs.
invariants.fixHint: Replace $use with a client extension: db.$extends({ query: { $allModels: { async $allOperations({ args, query }) { return query(args); } } } }). https://www.prisma.io/docs/guides/upgrade-prisma-orm/v7
invariants.avoid: This runs only when @prisma/client, or prisma when the client package is absent, is known to be at least 7.0.0. A lower bound below 7, including ^6, wins over a newer hoisted install. workspace:* counts only when the installed copy is 7 or newer. A $use value that is not called stays quiet.

source.paraphrase: The prisma-client generator, which is the default in Prisma ORM 7, has no Prisma.validator. TypeScript's satisfies keyword replaces it. The deprecated prisma-client-js generator still provides the helper.

invariants.why: A Prisma.validator call fails to typecheck against the default Prisma ORM 7 client, which no longer generates that function.
invariants.fixHint: Use satisfies instead of Prisma.validator, for example { email: true } satisfies Prisma.UserSelect. https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v7/prisma-schema/overview/generators
invariants.avoid: Warns only on Prisma 7 or newer. prisma-client-js still has Prisma.validator; this check cannot read the generator, so that deprecated generator still warns. A Prisma.validator reference that is not called stays quiet.

source.paraphrase: Prisma ORM 7 requires a driver adapter for every database when constructing PrismaClient. Accelerate is the documented exception and passes accelerateUrl with no adapter. The 7.0.0 changelog also removes the datasources and datasourceUrl constructor options.

invariants.why: A Prisma ORM 7 client constructed without a driver adapter cannot connect, and the old datasources and datasourceUrl options are no longer accepted.
invariants.fixHint: Pass a driver adapter: new PrismaClient({ adapter }). Accelerate uses new PrismaClient({ accelerateUrl }) and no adapter. https://www.prisma.io/docs/guides/upgrade-prisma-orm/v7
invariants.avoid: Warns only on Prisma 7 or newer. { adapter } and { accelerateUrl } pass, including quoted keys. A variable, call, spread, or nested adapter key stays quiet. Prisma 6 constructs without an adapter and stays quiet.
